title: Sketch Lifecycle Explorer
description: A slowed, steppable model of the p5.js sketch lifecycle: a falling-ball sketch is drawn one draw() statement at a time while counters show setup() calls, draw() calls and frameCount, and checkboxes that skip background() or move the ball before it show why statement order inside draw() changes the canvas.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: p5.js
Sketch Lifecycle
setup() and draw()
Animation Loop
publisher: MicroSims 2.0: Generating, Instrumenting and Evaluating Interactive Learning Objects with AI

educational.topic: The p5.js setup() and draw() lifecycle and drawing order
learningObjectives: The learner will explain when setup() and draw() run and why the order of statements inside draw() changes what appears on the canvas.
prerequisites: The p5.js Sketch, setup() Function and draw() Function sections (Chapter 6)

controls.label: Start / Pause
controls.action: Call draw() repeatedly at the chosen frame rate

controls.label: Step one frame
controls.action: Run exactly one draw() call, highlighting each statement as it runs

assumptions: The sketch's canvas is an offscreen buffer that persists between simulated frames, like a real p5.js canvas
frameCount equals the number of draw() calls
limitations: The draw loop is simulated and slowed; real p5.js aims for about 60 frames per second

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-observe-explain with a slowed, steppable loop
keyQuestions: How many times does setup() run? And draw()?
What would happen if background() were never called?
Why does the ball vanish when it is drawn before the background?
commonMisconceptions: Shapes drawn in an earlier frame are removed automatically
The order of statements inside draw() does not matter
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the canvas for a draw() with reordered statements
Explain a streak or a vanished shape from the statement order
